The bug has been fixed and verified.

### Cause

incorrectly by 1 instead of by the number of code units consumed (`c.length`), causing subsequent characters to be misaligned or omitted.

### Solution
- Set `len` to `input.length()`.
- When `consumed == 0`, advance `pos` by `c.length` (`Character.toChars(...)` length).
- When `consumed > 0`, advance `pos` by the number of code units of the consumed code points.
- Saved the patch as `negative_fix.patch`.

result.response:
The bug has been fixed and verified.

### Cause of the Bug
In [`CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence, Writer)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_17_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/translate/CharSequenceTranslator.java#L75-L104), loop termination was bound to the code point count `len = Character.codePointCount(input, 0, input.length())` rather than the character length `input.length()`, while position `pos` was advanced as character index and code point index inconsistently. When encountering a supplementary character (which consists of two Java `char`s / a surrogate pair), `pos` was incremented incorrectly by 1 instead of by the number of code units consumed (`c.length`), causing subsequent characters to be misaligned or omitted.

### Solution
- Set `len` to `input.length()`.
- When `consumed == 0`, advance `pos` by `c.length` (`Character.toChars(...)` length).
- When `consumed > 0`, advance `pos` by the number of code units of the consumed code points.
- Saved the patch as `negative_fix.patch`.
